title: Quiz: the Swift language
description: You have finished the Swift language half of the course. This review mixes questions from every module. If one stumps you, revisit that module before moving on to Xcode.

questions.question: Which is the best way to give back "no result" from a function that searches a list?

answers.text: Return an optional and nil when nothing is found

questions.why: Optionals say clearly that there may be no value, and Swift makes callers handle it.

questions.question: You change a property on a copy of a value. When does the original change too?
questions.why: Classes are references; structs are values.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.detail:
let words = ["swift", "is", "fun"]
print(words.filter { $0.count > 2 }.map { $0.uppercased() })
questions.why: filter keeps the longer words, then map uppercases them.

questions.question: Which keeps state safe when many tasks change it at once?
questions.why: Only one task can be inside an actor at a time.

questions.question: In Swift 6.4, what happens to a private var count = 0 in a struct's memberwise initializer?

answers.text: It is left out, and the initializer stays usable

questions.why: That is Swift 6.4's smarter memberwise initializer.

questions.question: Which type best models "a payment by cash, card (with its last four digits) or voucher (with a code)"?

answers.text: A struct with three optional properties

questions.why: Each case carries exactly its own data, and switches must handle all three.
